newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees no slippage on deficit goals - official.
newsitem.headline: France sees no slippage on deficit goals - official.

text.p: A finance ministry official said on Wednesday France would meet its target of reducing the public deficit to three percent of GDP this year -- one of the target criteria for joining European monetary union in January 1999 -- and said that there were no signs of slippage in public finances.

The official was reacting to a report in afternoon daily Le Monde which said measures beyond those foreseen could be needed to meet the deficit goal due to signs of weak government revenue and dangers of a social security deficit exceeding forecasts.
"The government will achieve its objectives, that is, three percent," said the official.
The official pointed to the announcement on Tuesday that the budget deficit at the end of February was 72.4 billion francs, versus 90 billion at the same stage last year.
Nothing so far cast any doubt on the government's aims, said the official, adding that in any case the government "will do what is necessary".

Le Monde said that in advance of a May parliamentary debate on the 1998 budget, the budget and forecasting divisions of the finance ministry had presented simulations to the government which hinted that the deficit this year could overshoot the three percent target fairly markedly.

It noted that such warnings on budget pressure are customary in the run-up to parliamentary debates on the following year's finances but said people in "government circles" were not hiding the fact that the government might have to consider tightening the screws a bit further in coming months.
